# Program Guide

## Overview

The Dover Tigers strength and conditioning program runs all year. Each phase has one main goal and builds on the one before it.

| Phase | When | Goal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Phase 0: Transition & Pre-Testing Prep | Oct 26 to Dec 13, 2026 | Recover from the season, then ramp back into training |
| Phase 1: Winter | Dec 14, 2026 to Feb 26, 2027 | Build max strength and muscle |
| Phase 2: Spring | Mar 1 to May 21, 2027 | Turn that strength into speed and power |
| Phase 2–3 Bridge | May 25 to Jun 15, 2027 | Keep training through the gap before summer |
| Phase 3: Early Summer | Jun 21 to Jul 29, 2027 | Speed and conditioning |
| Camp Bridge | Blackout week through the season opener | Keep your strength through camp |
| Phase 4: In-Season | The regular season | Hold on to your strength and power while you play |

**When we lift.** During the school year, sessions start at 3:30 PM on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday.

**Your numbers.** Most lifts are a percentage of your estimated one-rep max (e1RM). You test a 5-rep max (5RM) in Testing Week and at each retest, and the app turns it into your e1RM (5RM ÷ 0.87) and works out your weights for every set. Log your sets on the This Week tab.

**RPE (how hard a set felt).** Some work is set by effort instead of a percentage:

| RPE | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| 10 | Max effort. You could not have done another rep |
| 8–9 | 1–2 reps left in the tank |
| 6–7 | Hard, but several reps left and form still clean |
| 3–5 | Light. Technique work |

**If something hurts,** stop and tell the athletic trainer. Coaches don't diagnose or clear anyone.

## Phase 0 — Transition & Pre-Testing Prep

**Goal:** recover from the season, then ramp back into training so you show up to Testing Week ready to set a real 5RM.

- **Weeks 1–5 (Oct 26 to Nov 29): recovery.** No training and nothing expected.
- **Prep sessions (Nov 30 to Dec 11):** optional and coach-run, Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday at 3:30 PM, about 30–35 minutes. They start with bodyweight work, bring back the empty bar for technique, add light barbell touches, and finish with a short movement screen the Thursday and Friday before Testing Week.
- **Never heavy.** Every barbell rep in Prep stays at RPE 6 or below. The point is to move well, not to find your max early.
- **The four-session rule.** If you attend fewer than four Prep sessions, you won't take a heavy 5RM in Testing Week. You'll work up to one solid set of 5 instead, and test for real at the Week 6 retest.

## Phase 1 — Winter

**Goal:** build max strength and muscle. This is the base everything else is built on.

- **Testing Week (Dec 14 to 18):** Monday squat, Tuesday bench press and pull-up, Thursday deadlift, Friday overhead press and make-ups.
- **The week:** Day A Squat (Monday), Day B Hinge (Tuesday), Day C Push (Thursday), Day D Pull and single-leg work (Friday).
- **Main lifts:** 4 sets of 5 at 75–85% of your e1RM, then a lighter back-off set, followed by an accessory circuit.
- **Lighter weeks:** Weeks 2, 4 and 8 are 3-set weeks. **Peak weeks:** Weeks 5 and 9 are 4 sets of 4 at 85%. **Retest:** Week 6 (Feb 1 to 5).
- **Winter Break** (Dec 21 to Jan 3) has no training. On the three Mondays with no school (Jan 18, Feb 8, Feb 15), Day A moves to Tuesday and Day B to Wednesday.
- **Playing basketball or wrestling?** You may be on the Multi-Sport track: 2 days a week, same weights, no accessory circuit.

## Phase 2 — Spring

**Goal:** turn your winter strength into speed and power you can use on the field.

- **Testing Week (Mar 1 to 5):** same layout as Phase 1, plus a vertical jump on Monday.
- **Every day has two parts.** The **Strength Lane** is heavy main-lift work. The **Power Lane** is lighter weight moved as fast as you can: trap bar jump squat, trap bar jump shrug, speed bench press, and a rotational press or med-ball throw.
- **Loaded jumps** need a landing check with a coach first. Until you pass it, you do the same jump without weight.
- **Spring Break** (Mar 26 to Apr 2) has no training, and the week after it is lighter.
- **Retest:** Week 7 (Apr 19 to 23).

## Phase 2–3 Bridge

**Goal:** keep training through the gap between the end of Phase 2 and summer, so nobody shows up to summer testing cold.

- **When:** Tuesdays and Fridays, May 25 to Jun 15, 2027.
- **What:** two sessions a week at about the weights you finished Phase 2 with. Voluntary.

## Phase 3 — Early Summer

**Goal:** speed and conditioning, once school is out and you have full days.

- **Four days a week (Monday to Thursday),** each followed by a football practice segment.
- **The week:** Monday acceleration and sled pulls, Tuesday tempo runs and skills, Wednesday an upper-body maintenance lift, Thursday jumps and sprint conditioning.
- **Test Week (Jun 21 to 24):** 40-yard dash and 10- and 20-yard splits Monday, 300-yard shuttle Tuesday. **Retest Week (Jul 26 to 29)** repeats both tests so you can see what you gained.
- **Heat:** coaches check the heat reading before every outdoor session and can shorten, move or cancel work. Drink water all day, not just at practice.
- **New to the program** (incoming freshmen and other first-timers)? You start here, with technique sessions before any heavy lifting or testing.

## Camp Bridge

**Goal:** keep your strength through blackout week and camp, so the season opener isn't a cold start.

- **No lifting** in the first five days of camp, while everyone gets used to the heat.
- Once two practices a day begin, there is **one short lift a week.** Conditioning happens at the end of practice.

## Phase 4 — In-Season

**Goal:** keep your strength and power through the season without wearing you down.

- **Two short lifts a week** (about 30–40 minutes): squat and bench on the first lift day, deadlift and pull-up on the second. 3 sets of 3–5 reps at 80–85% of your e1RM. The lift days move with the game schedule.
- **Squat and deadlift ease back in:** your first two sessions of each are lighter.
- **Rate every session.** After every practice, lift and game, rate how hard it was from 0 to 10 in the app. Coaches use it to watch your weekly load.

## Injury Prevention

These four pieces run in every phase. They take a few minutes, and they are some of the most important minutes of the session.

- **NMT warm-up.** A short warm-up before every session (about 7 minutes during the lifting phases, longer in the summer field phase): planks, balance work, landing practice, the neck holds and two build-up sprints. It trains the balance and body control that help protect your knees and ankles.
- **Nordic hamstring curl.** 2 sets, twice a week, after the lift (Day B and Day D in Phases 1 and 2). Reps build from 4–6 up to 8–10 as the weeks go on. It strengthens your hamstrings to help prevent pulls when you sprint. More than mild soreness the next day, tightness while sprinting, or slower sprints? Skip it and tell the athletic trainer.
- **Neck 4-way holds.** Press your own hand against your forehead, the back of your head and each side, and hold 6–8 seconds each way. Steady pressure only, no jerking, and it should never hurt. Neck pain or a recent head or neck injury means you see the athletic trainer first.
- **Shoulder finisher.** Face pulls or band pull-aparts, 2 sets of 15–20, after every session. Light work that keeps your shoulders healthy alongside all the pressing.
